title: The Hellenistic Kingdoms
objective: After this level you can describe the kingdoms of Alexander's generals.
summary: After Ipsus in 301 BCE, Alexander’s empire settled into Macedonian-ruled kingdoms: the Ptolemies in Egypt, the Seleucids in Asia and the Antigonids in Macedonia.

cards.headline: One of Alexander’s generals traded land in India for 500 elephants.
cards.body: It turned out to be a bargain. The elephants helped decide who got Alexander’s empire.

cards.headline: Elephants decide it
cards.body: Seleucus gave up territory to the Indian ruler Chandragupta for 500 elephants. At Ipsus in 301 BCE, Seleucus and his allies faced another general, Antigonus. Seleucus had an estimated 400 elephants, and they made the difference. Antigonus was killed, and with him went any hope of putting Alexander’s empire back together.

items.label: Ptolemies
points: The last to fall to Rome, in 30 BCE

items.label: Seleucids
points: From Thrace to India’s border at their peak
Capital Antioch; ended by Rome in 64 BCE

mascot.line: You don’t need every date here. Remember the three families and where each ruled.

cards.headline: Greek at the top
cards.body: All three royal families came from Alexander’s Macedonian generals, and they ruled many different peoples. In their kingdoms Greek became the language of government, and Greek culture mixed with the cultures of the peoples they ruled. Picture a head office where every memo is in Greek, whether the branch office sits on the Nile or in Syria.

cards.headline: The Hellenistic kingdoms
learned: Seleucids from Thrace to India’s border

questions.prompt: Which family ruled Macedonia after Alexander’s empire split?

options.label: The Seleucids
options.rationale: They ruled from Thrace to India’s border.

questions.explanation: The Antigonids ruled Macedonia from 306 to 168 BCE.

questions.prompt: Why was the Battle of Ipsus in 301 BCE a turning point for Alexander’s empire?

options.label: Alexander was killed there
options.rationale: He had died in Babylon in 323 BCE.

options.label: It ended the last real hope of reuniting it
Porus’s elephants won it for India

questions.explanation: Antigonus was killed at Ipsus, and with him any hope of reuniting the empire.

questions.prompt: Level 1 ends the Hellenistic age in 30 BCE. Which kingdom fell to Rome that year?
questions.explanation: Ptolemaic Egypt was the last Hellenistic kingdom, taken by Rome in 30 BCE.
